issue: NAI img2img must use an editable target resolution and both img2img and redraw must restore the original pixel extent

before.reproduction: Add an NAI img2img control for a layer, expand it, and try to type a custom target width or adapt one side to the source aspect ratio; also redraw a canvas larger than 2048 pixels on one side.
before.expected: Width and height are editable, snap to the nearest legal 64-pixel grid after Enter or focus loss, auto-fill on layer selection, and can auto-adapt the other side to the source ratio. Each side remains at most 2048 and total pixels remain at most 3145728. Img2img and redraw stretch to the request target and stretch back to the exact original extent and offset.
before.actual: The target was a three-item Normal-preset combo box. Custom dimensions and aspect adaptation were unavailable, and ordinary redraw retained a separate approximately 3MP request policy instead of the requested 1MP-to-2048 edit policy.

adjacent_working_case: NAI text generation keeps its existing provider request limit, and selection inpaint without an img2img base remains an infill request with a mask.
hypothesis: Fixed-preset normalization in the control model, combo-box-only UI, and request conversion prevents custom targets, while redraw lacks an explicit source/target extent pair at the NAI boundary.
disproof: The hypothesis would be false if arbitrary dimensions were already persisted and snapped only on commit, or if ordinary redraw already carried a distinct NAI target and restored provider-sized results to the source extent.
